Alchemy provides the tech that allows users to issue virtual payment cards to AI bots embedded with a slate of restrictions, such as spending limits and the types of products that may be purchased. The company's AgentCard will support Mastercard payment credentials through an integration with Mastercard AgentPay, giving developers a simple way to build AI agents that can safely complete purchases for users online, Alchemy said.

that cardholders can choose where in the payments process authorization takes place. For example, a user can authorize a transaction based on preset parameters in advance, letting the agent proceed, or ask it to check before making the purchase.

The two companies are teaming up as a wide range of payment companies prepare for a new era in payments, where AI bots increasingly control purchases. That looming scenario will require banks, merchants, and payment processors to rethink fraud- and crime-detection systems already in place.

"AI agents are quickly moving from simple assistants to software that can take action for people," said Nikil Viswanathan, co-founder and CEO of Alchemy. "To make that possible in everyday commerce, agents need a trusted way to pay, prove authorization, and operate within clear user-defined limits."
stock slipped 0.3% in Thursday morning trading.

title: Mastercard links up with Alchemy to offer agentic shopping option
